He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska Cornhuskers]]. ==High school career== McGowens played basketball for [[Wren High School]] in [[Piedmont, South Carolina]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 26.3 points, 3.8 rebounds and three assists per game, and was named Region 1-4A Player of the Year. He led his team to a Class 4A Upper State runner-up finish.{{cite web |last1=Keepfer |first1=Scott |title=Wren High basketball standout Bryce McGowens won't require surgery on wrist |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/2019/02/23/bryce-mcgowens-wrist-injury-surgery-wren-high-ridge-view/2964687002/ |website=[[The Greenville News]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=February 23, 2019}} In his junior season, McGowens scored a school-record 65 points in a second round win at the Class 4A playoffs.{{cite web |last1=Preston |first1=Geoff |title=Wren star and Florida State commit Bryce McGowens drops 65 points as Hurricanes advance |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/02/23/wren-basketball-and-fsu-commit-bryce-mcgowens-scores-65-hurricanes-advance-schsl-playoffs/4791334002/ |website=[[The Greenville News]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=February 23, 2020}} He averaged 25.3 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game as a junior, leading his team to the Class 4A Upper State championship game and repeating as Region 1-4A Player of the Year. For his senior season, McGowens moved to Legacy Early College in [[Greenville, South Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Smith III |first1=Kennington Lloyd |title=Top basketball prospect Bryce McGowens to transfer to Legacy Early College for senior year |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2020/04/20/wrens-bryce-mcgowens-transfer-legacy-early-college/5163155002/ |website=[[Anderson Independent-Mail]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=April 20, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 21.6 points, 4.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game, earning South Carolina [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] honors.{{cite web |last1=Paniagua |first1=Hunter |title=Husker recruit Bryce McGowens is South Carolina's Gatorade player of the year |url=https://omaha.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/husker-recruit-bryce-mcgowens-is-south-carolinas-gatorade-player-of-the-year/article_cfcedd5e-c54f-11eb-83db-4b4089cbc298.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=June 4, 2021}} He was selected to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] roster.{{cite web |title=Bryce McGowens – 2021–22 – Men's Basketball |url=https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/bryce-mcgowens/42989 |website=University of Nebraska Athletics |access-date=June 29, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== McGowens was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and a four-star recruit by [[ESPN]]. On February 10, 2020, he announced his commitment to play college basketball for [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web |last1=Smith III |first1=Kennington Lloyd |title=Here's why Wren's Bryce McGowens picked Florida State over Clemson, Xavier and others |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/2020/02/10/wren-four-star-bryce-mcgowens-commits-florida-state-basketball/4712499002/ |website=[[Anderson Independent-Mail]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=February 10, 2020}} On October 8, 2020, McGowens decommitted from the program.{{cite web |last1=Weiler |first1=Curt |title=Five-star shooting guard Bryce McGowens decommits from Florida State |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/story/sports/college/fsu/mensbasketball/2020/10/08/florida-state-fsu-basketball-recruiting-seminoles-bryce-mcgowens-decommit-five-star-leonard-hamilton/5923288002/ |website=[[Tallahassee Democrat]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=October 8, 2020}} On November 13, 2020, he committed to [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]], becoming the highest-ranked recruit in program history and its first five-star recruit.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Bryce McGowens (No. 33) becomes Nebraska's highest-ranked commit |work=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |date=March 6, 2022}} McGowens was named to the Third Team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] as well as the All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} He averaged 16.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game. On March 21, 2022, McGowens declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Nebraska Cornhuskers freshman Bryce McGowens to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33564381/nebraska-cornhuskers-freshman-bryce-mcgowens-declare-nba-draft |access-date=March 21, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=March 21, 2022}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] | 31 || 31 || 33.3 || .403 || .274 || .831 || 5.2 || 1.4 || .7 || .3 || 16.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== McGowens' older brother, Trey, played college basketball for [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]] before transferring to Nebraska.{{cite web |last1=Smith III |first1=Kennington Lloyd |title=Brothers Bryce, Trey McGowens' lifelong dream will play out through Nebraska basketball |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/11/20/heres-how-after-13-years-mcgowens-brothers-became-teammates-again-nebraska-legacy-early-college/6309739002/ |website=[[The Greenville News]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=November 20, 2020}} His father, Bobby, was a two-sport athlete in basketball and football at [[South Carolina State Bulldogs and Lady Bulldogs|South Carolina State]] after playing football at [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]]. McGowens' mother, Pam, played basketball for [[Western Carolina Catamounts women's basketball|Western Carolina]]. Both of his parents have coached high school basketball.{{cite web |last1=Keepfer |first1=Scott |title=Here are tips from the McGowens basketball family on how to navigate a busy schedule |url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/clemson/2019/02/11/life-basketball-how-mcgowens-family-makes-busy-schedule-work/2741476002/ |website=[[The Greenville News]] |access-date=June 29, 2021 |date=February 11, 2019}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://huskers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/bryce-mcgowens/42989 Nebraska Cornhuskers bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:McGowens, Bryce}} [[Category:2002 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from South Carolina]] [[Category:People from Pendleton, South Carolina]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
